generator: stub.py, driver.py and run_lane.sh were written by hand for HAMCP-297 (no generator). TOPOLOGY in stub.py is static and synthetic.

node_dumps.method: Copied byte-for-byte from the source commit; not edited. stub.py refuses to start on a hash mismatch (PINNED_DUMPS).

residuals: The stub applies write_attribute to its own attribute cache and reports it back. Upstream TestNodeCommandHandler.ts:187-190 only logs the write and returns success with no actual write. A lane on this stub proves the Core-side command and the read-back path, not a real device write.
get_network_topology returns static synthetic content (stub.py TOPOLOGY). Core forwards whatever the Matter Server builds, so a lane proves pass-through and projection, not topology construction.
server_info_schema_version takes effect for Core only after a reconnect, because Core caches schema_version at connect.
statement: Test-only lane asset: a Matter Server stub (server side of a WebSocket subset), the lane driver, the runner, and three Matter node dumps. Never a product path. No live Home Assistant, deployed MCP endpoint, production credential or secret was used; the driver generates random disposable onboarding credentials inside the disposable Core container and never prints them.
